chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The boy, when death presents itself to him, so he bequeaths and has not attained awareness (puberty), his bequest is valid for the relatives and is not valid for the strangers.'

key_terms.الْغُلَامَ: The boy (specifically one who has not reached full maturity/puberty in this context)
key_terms.حَضَرَهُ الْمَوْتُ: Death presented itself to him / was near death
key_terms.ذَوِي الْأَرْحَامِ: The relatives (specifically collateral kin beyond the direct heirs)
key_terms.لِلْغُرَبَاءِ: For the strangers (non-relatives or those outside the immediate family circle)

ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a pre-pubescent boy's bequest for relatives versus strangers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal capacity of a pre-pubescent boy (ghulam) nearing death to make a bequest, distinguishing between inheritance for close kin (dhawi al-arham) and strangers (al-ghuraba'). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights that while such a boy lacks full legal maturity, his bequest is valid for relatives but limited in scope, reflecting the principle that their estate is primarily reserved for their direct lineage rather than external parties.
